niche_preference_profile: This user consistently prefers interfaces with strong, obvious structure: clear information hierarchy, prominent primary actions, modular card-based organization, and readable contrast. They often like spacious layouts with breathing room, rounded containers, and polished card treatments. They frequently respond well to richer, more complete content when it is well organized, but reject dense or cluttered presentations that flatten hierarchy. Their color preference is mixed by context, but they repeatedly favor controlled, polished palettes with good contrast, often dark navy/purple or light neutral themes over harsher, noisier, or low-contrast alternatives.

top_7_criteria.description: Prefers very clear hierarchy with dominant titles or focal content, visible subtitles/section labels, strong separation between content levels, and unmistakable emphasis on the primary action.
Prefers open, airy layouts with generous spacing, breathing room, and fewer tightly packed elements; rejects cramped, compressed, or overly dense arrangements.
Prefers content organized into distinct cards, rows, or grouped modules with clear boundaries instead of monolithic panels, flat lists, or unstructured continuous layouts.
Prefers highly visible, clearly prioritized actions such as full-width or strongly emphasized buttons, with primary actions easy to find and secondary actions visually quieter.
Prefers softer, more rounded corners on cards, modals, and controls, often paired with pill buttons and a gentler overall component shape language.
Prefers strong text readability, clear contrast between foreground and background, and visual separation that makes content and controls easy to parse.
Prefers fuller, more complete screens with visible details, labels, metrics, and support information when they are presented in an organized, scannable way rather than as clutter.
